newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's engineers suspend pay protest.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's engineers suspend pay protest.

text.p: Jordan's engineering union has suspended plans for a strike on Saturday after Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti promised to address grievances of all professional unions, a union official said on Wednesday.

The official said Saturday's limited strike would be postponed for two months to give Kabariti time to carry out his pledge. A special committee including union vice president Hosni Abu Ghida and two ministers has been formed to look into the pay demands, he said.
"The prime minister said all professional unions would be satisfied," the union official said.

He said the decision to suspend protests was taken on Tuesday by the general assembly of the Islamist-dominated Engineers' Union, which has 26,000 members and is by far the most powerful and vocal in Jordan.
The engineers say the government has failed to implement an October pay accord. They had threatened to escalate to an all-out strike on March 22 if their demands were not met.
